description: Return exactly 10 cities. If cities are tied at the 10th place, keep an arbitrary subset of them.

b.request: Group addresses by city ID, count the addresses in each city, divide each count by the average count across city IDs appearing in the address table, and divide each count by the total number of addresses; return the 10 city IDs with the highest shares in descending order, breaking ties arbitrarily and leaving all values unrounded
b.sql: WITH city_counts AS (SELECT city_id, COUNT(*) AS address_count FROM address GROUP BY city_id) SELECT city_id, address_count, address_count / AVG(address_count) OVER () AS count_to_average, address_count / SUM(address_count) OVER () AS share_of_addresses FROM city_counts ORDER BY share_of_addresses DESC LIMIT 10

a.request: For each `city_id` in the address table, show the city ID, its number of addresses, that count divided by the average number of addresses per city, and that count as a share of all addresses (count divided by the total number of addresses). Rank cities by that share from highest to lowest and return exactly 10 rows, breaking any ties at 10th place arbitrarily, without rounding.
a.sql: WITH city_counts AS (SELECT city_id, COUNT(*) AS address_count FROM address GROUP BY city_id), totals AS (SELECT AVG(address_count) AS avg_addresses_per_city, SUM(address_count) AS total_addresses FROM city_counts) SELECT c.city_id, c.address_count, c.address_count / t.avg_addresses_per_city AS count_to_city_average, c.address_count / t.total_addresses AS share_of_all_addresses FROM city_counts AS c CROSS JOIN totals AS t ORDER BY share_of_all_addresses DESC LIMIT 10

c.request: For each city in the address table, show its city ID, how many addresses it has, that count relative to the average number of addresses per city, and its share of all addresses. Which are the top 10 cities by that share, highest first? Don't round anything. Return exactly 10 cities. If cities are tied at the 10th place, keep an arbitrary subset of them.
c.sql: WITH city_counts AS (SELECT city_id, COUNT(*) AS address_count FROM address GROUP BY city_id) SELECT city_id, address_count, address_count / AVG(address_count) OVER () AS relative_to_average, address_count / SUM(address_count) OVER () AS share_of_all_addresses FROM city_counts ORDER BY share_of_all_addresses DESC LIMIT 10

d.request: For each city in the address table, show its city ID, address count, that count relative to the average address count per city, and its share of all addresses. Return exactly the 10 cities with the highest shares, in descending order, choosing arbitrarily among cities tied for 10th place. Do not round any values.
d.sql: WITH city_counts AS (SELECT city_id, COUNT(*) AS address_count FROM address GROUP BY city_id) SELECT city_id, address_count, address_count / AVG(address_count) OVER () AS relative_to_average, address_count / SUM(address_count) OVER () AS share_of_all_addresses FROM city_counts ORDER BY share_of_all_addresses DESC LIMIT 10
